title: This Beetle Fires Near-Boiling Spray 500 Times a Second
subject: bombardier beetle

scenes.text: This beetle has a chemical weapon, and it fires it from its rear.
Inside its body, two chemicals sit apart: hydrogen peroxide and hydroquinone. Mixed, they explode.
The reaction heats the spray to near a hundred degrees Celsius. That's almost boiling water.
It doesn't fire once. It pulses about 500 times every second, like a tiny machine gun.
Pulsing keeps the beetle's own body from being cooked by one big blast.
A boiling chemical machine gun, from an insect you could hold on a fingertip.

description:
The bombardier beetle mixes two chemicals inside its body and sprays the near-boiling result.
It fires in rapid pulses, about 500 every second.
Would you pick one of these up?
first_comment: Scientists say the pulse rate runs from about 370 to 735 a second depending on the beetle. Which animal weapon would you want?
